title: Pete Fontaine and Lawrence Welk's band
summary: Opinions on Pete Fontaine's musicianship and role with Welk.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience

blocks.x: Pete Fontaine. That boy couldn't read music, couldn't they? Teaching me music right now with Lawrence Welk. He can't sit in the men no more than me. That's out of his class altogether. He's a good clown at man in his own category. But when he gets in to play with the other guys, there's a difference in life and day. You know that. He's a good clown at play. But there's some men in Lawrence Welk's band could play just as good as him. They got him up there for a purpose. They got him only for recording. To make records. Did you know that? Lawrence Welk was to make this jazz record. Dixie Rand song. That's right. That's right. Even got him playing with those little folk. He'd sing it, making the records. Them little girls. Little girls, yeah. And he'd play the car on that outside while they're making records together. What about all that? Pete, he ought to take that whiskey off. He got a toupee over his head. Yeah. He was bald in him and he got a toupee. That's good. But still grows them whiskers.
